clusters.label: Covalent bonding
clusters.definition: Chemical bonding characterized by electron sharing between bonded atoms.
clusters.reason: All denote covalent bonding character. Different bonded species, materials, diagnostic methods and assertion strengths remain attached to their claims.

clusters.label: Semiconductor behavior from calculated band structure
clusters.definition: Semiconducting electronic structure identified through a calculated band gap.
clusters.reason: All describe calculated semiconducting band structures; directness, gap values and dimensionality belong to the respective material claims.

clusters.label: Semiconductor behavior associated with hopping conduction
clusters.definition: Semiconducting transport behavior attributed to activated small-polaron and variable-range hopping.
clusters.reason: The evidence identifies transport behavior through hopping mechanisms, rather than a calculated band-gap classification.

clusters.label: Composite Seebeck coefficient
clusters.definition: The thermoelectric voltage response per temperature difference of a composite.
clusters.reason: Both denote the composite's Seebeck coefficient itself. Opposite changes and different constituent materials remain claim attributes; neither explicitly identifies a distinct ionic or thermogalvanic coefficient.

clusters.label: Excellent stability under stretching and thermal cycling
clusters.definition: Stability of the engineered LCE ionic thermoelectric materials during cyclic stretching, long-term testing and temperature-controlled cycling.
clusters.reason: The evidence specifies the stability tests and material scope.

unresolved.reason: Stability in wearable textiles is asserted without identifying the maintained property or testing conditions, preventing equivalence with the specified LCE stability.

clusters.label: Photothermal conversion performance
clusters.definition: Performance in converting incident light into heat.
clusters.reason: Both refer to the same conversion function; absorber thickness and film properties are separate claim contexts.

clusters.label: Strain
clusters.definition: Mechanical deformation used to control the s(II)-to-s(I) phase transition.
clusters.reason: Strain is clearly identified as the applied control condition for the phase transition.

unresolved.reason: Enhanced strain does not specify whether this means deformation, strain capacity or failure strain; equivalence with applied strain is undetermined.

clusters.label: Elevated temperature
clusters.definition: A temperature condition higher than the reference or lower-temperature conditions of a study.
clusters.reason: All denote the generic higher-temperature condition, without specifying distinct temperature regimes. Materials, methods and resulting changes remain separate.

clusters.label: PEDOT:PSS thermoelectric performance
clusters.definition: The performance of PEDOT:PSS in thermoelectric conversion.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly concern the same polymer's thermoelectric performance; doping and treatment strategies describe how it is changed.

clusters.label: Plasticity of Ag2Te/Ag2S composites
clusters.definition: Plastic deformation capability of Ag2Te/Ag2S composites, assessed through bending strain.
clusters.reason: The evidence reports composite bending performance, distinct from the calculated mechanical responses elsewhere.

clusters.label: Plasticity of Cu/Gr stacking configurations
clusters.definition: Calculated plastic deformation capability of Cu/double-layer graphene/Cu structures.
clusters.reason: The property is explicitly associated with the Gr-Hollow versus Gr-Top stacking configurations.

clusters.label: Plasticity of zinc-blende alloys
clusters.definition: Plastic deformation capability inferred from first-principles mechanical calculations for zinc-blende MgxZn1−xSySe1−y and its constituent compounds.
clusters.reason: This is a bulk alloy mechanical property, distinct from the specified layered and interfacial configurations.

clusters.label: Plasticity of Al/Graphite interface configurations
clusters.definition: Deformation capacity of Al/Graphite interface configurations, characterized by sustainable maximum strain.
clusters.reason: The evidence specifically ties interfacial plasticity to Top versus Bridge configurations and Al–C ionic bonding.

clusters.label: p-type semiconducting character in dried cement composites
clusters.definition: The p-type semiconducting response reported for dried CNT-reinforced cement composites containing pristine SrTiO3 nanoparticles.
clusters.reason: This is a reported sample response with explicit drying and filler qualifiers.

clusters.label: Predicted p-type semiconducting character
clusters.definition: P-type semiconducting character predicted for ZnCrX2 chalcopyrites through transport calculations.
clusters.reason: The evidence explicitly identifies a computational prediction, distinguished from the reported composite response.

clusters.label: Figure of merit close to unity
clusters.definition: A calculated thermoelectric figure of merit approximately equal to one.
clusters.reason: Both describe the same predicted thermoelectric quantity and approximate value; material dimensionality and room-temperature qualification remain attached to individual claims.

clusters.label: Orthorhombic structure
clusters.definition: Crystal structure belonging to the orthorhombic crystal system.
clusters.reason: All denote the same crystallographic classification, without implying identical compositions, dopants or detailed atomic structures.

clusters.label: Undoped CaMnO3
clusters.definition: Unsubstituted CaMnO3 described as lacking Mn3+ and the associated Jahn–Teller distortion.
clusters.reason: The evidence identifies undoped CaMnO3 but does not establish the nanostructured sample qualifier of the other member.

clusters.label: Undoped nanostructured CaMnO3
clusters.definition: The undoped CaMnO3 reference in the nanostructured lanthanide-substitution study.
clusters.reason: The title and nanoparticle comparison supply a sample qualifier that must be retained; cross-paper sample equivalence is not established.

clusters.label: Point defects
clusters.definition: Localized defects at individual atomic sites in a solid.
clusters.reason: Both labels denote the general point-defect class. Dopants, host compositions and preparation conditions remain with their claims; no identical defect species is inferred.

clusters.label: Intended improvement of Seebeck coefficient
clusters.definition: A targeted improvement in the Seebeck coefficient through modification of electronic structure.
clusters.reason: The relation explicitly describes an intended, hypothetical improvement rather than an observed outcome.

clusters.label: Improved Seebeck coefficient
clusters.definition: A reported beneficial change in the Seebeck coefficient relative to a comparison state.
clusters.reason: Both report improvement of the same quantity. Neither is normalized to a numerical increase, because the evidence does not establish a common signed direction.

clusters.label: Modified electronic structure in Sm- or La-doped Sr2TiO4
clusters.definition: Electronic-structure modification associated with separate Sm or La doping of Sr2TiO4.
clusters.reason: The modification is tied to specified dopants and carrier injection; its detailed nature is not shown equivalent to cage-center doping.

clusters.label: Modified electronic structure from lanthanide cage-center doping
clusters.definition: Electronic-structure modification produced by placing a heavy lanthanide at the pnictogen-cage center in filled skutterudites.
clusters.reason: The evidence specifies a distinct doping location and computational context; shared thermoelectric benefits do not establish an identical modification.

clusters.label: Indirect band gap
clusters.definition: An electronic band gap whose valence-band maximum and conduction-band minimum occur at different crystal momenta.
clusters.reason: All identify the same calculated band-gap type. Semiconductor versus insulator classification and material composition do not change indirectness.

clusters.label: Optical anisotropy
clusters.definition: Dependence of optical response on direction or polarization.
clusters.reason: All denote the same calculated optical property; pressure, photon-energy range and material identity remain claim conditions.

clusters.label: High optical absorption coefficient
clusters.definition: A comparatively large coefficient describing attenuation of light by absorption.
clusters.reason: Both describe high calculated optical absorption in the visible-to-ultraviolet region, rather than an increase relative to a baseline.

clusters.label: Solar cells and optoelectronic devices
clusters.definition: The application category comprising solar cells and devices involving optical and electronic functions.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly name the same proposed application category; different candidate materials and reflectivity characteristics do not alter that category.
